evals.prompt: Design a skill that Codex will load from our team plugin to draft release notes from merged pull requests. Give me the SKILL.md frontmatter and a short outline of the body, and don't create any files.
evals.expected_output: Standard Agent Skills frontmatter and a short body outline for a Codex plugin skill, based on Codex-specific guidance only, with no files created.
assertions: Reads the authoring skill's Codex reference, references/codex.md
Does not read the omp or Claude references, references/omp.md or references/claude.md
Uses only standard Agent Skills frontmatter fields, without omp- or Claude-only fields such as `hide` or `argument-hint`
Mentions keeping the main SKILL.md within Codex's 8,000-byte plugin-skill limit or measuring its size

evals.prompt: Revise this agent skill instruction: 'Check manifest format yourself, then decide whether the guidance is useful.' The repository already pins validator example-validator 1.2.0 in package.json and runs it as `npx example-validator --config validator.json`; validator.json checks manifest format. Delegate the format check to that existing command while retaining semantic judgment. Do not introduce a wrapper.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the existing pinned validator and distinguishes format validation from semantic judgment.
assertions: Reuses the existing pinned validator and distinguishes format validation from semantic judgment.

evals.prompt: Review this portable agent skill manifest and its scope: `name: ticket-draft`, `description: Draft issue titles and bodies from supplied observations`, `allowed-tools: Bash`. Its intended job is drafting issues, not publishing them. No target client is specified; decide what metadata can be justified without assuming one.
evals.expected_output: Avoids inventing an intended client or client-specific metadata.
assertions: Avoids inventing an intended client or client-specific metadata.
